sections.overview: Dicrocoelium dendriticum is a parasitic flatworm, commonly called the lancet fluke, living as an adult in mammalian bile ducts.
sections.identification: Adults taper at both ends; thick-shelled eggs pass already embryonated in faeces.
sections.habitat: Adults inhabit the bile ducts of definitive hosts, usually grazing ruminants; the immature stages develop in terrestrial snails and ants.
sections.diet: It is parasitic: adults occupy bile ducts, while larvae develop inside intermediate hosts.
sections.behavior: Transmission depends on an infected ant being eaten by a definitive host; humans can become accidental hosts after swallowing infected ants on contaminated food.
sections.reproduction: Eggs leave an infected mammal in faeces, are taken up by a land snail, and pass through larval stages before reaching an ant and then another grazing host.
sections.ecology: The life cycle links pasture food webs across three hosts: a ruminant, a land snail and an ant, with Formica among common ant hosts.
sections.conservation: Heavy infections may cause biliary or liver complications, while most infections with few flukes have no overt symptoms.
